newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 7.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc seems to be on the brink of a big shift in its operating system strategy, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.
Other top stories included:
- AK Steel Holding Corp is thinking about building a steel processing plant in Ohio or Indiana.
- CSX Corp raised its bid for Conrail Inc as rival Norfolk Southern Corp considered doing the same.
- Dominion Resources Inc confirmed it was planning a bid to buy East Midlands Electricity Plc.
- Intel Corp foresaw revenues for its fourth quarter to be higher than those for the third.
- Texaco Inc suspended two executives for racial discrimination and conspiring to destroy documents.
- A federal judge has prevented the mayor of New York from airing News Corp Ltd's Fox News on a city cable channel.
- The head of Union Pacific Corp's railroad division has resigned.
- Mobil Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group plan to join their California exploration and production units.
- Loctite Corp asked its shareholders to wait for an evaluation before acting on Henkel KGaA's tender offer.
- Siemens AG reported a nearly 20-percent jump in profit for is latest fiscal year.
- Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp's quarterly net income rose 17 percent.
- Nynex shareholders approved going ahead with its $23 billion plan to be bought by Bell Atlantic Corp.
- Wallace Computer Services Inc shareholders rejected a proposal to limit the board of directors' ability to a "just-say-no" takeover defense.
- DreamWorks plans to build an $8 billion film-studio complex and technology center might be having problems.
- United Automobile Workers union supported a tentative labor agreement with General Motors Corp.
- The Dow Jones industrial average closed 1.6 percent higher after Election Day.
- United Steelworkers achieved many of its goals under a tentative labor pact with Bridgestone/Firestone.
- Wall Street is wondering if Concert Inc will perform better in the market than the stocks of MCI Communications and British Telecommunications.
- The bond market ended lower rather than higher following the outcome of the country's presidential elections because traders had anticipated President Bill Clinton's re-election.
-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610
